steps.title: Across the government, full releases fell from 41.6% to 9.5%
text: A closed request ends in one of 12 ways. Four are drawn here, each as a share of all requests closed that year. Released in full fell from 41.6% in FY2008 to 9.5% in FY2025; partly released went from 17.8% to 37.7% and no records found from 15.2% to 29.7%.
The curve is uneven. Is this one pattern shared across agencies, or a few large agencies moving the total?

steps.title: DHS now closes 6 in 10 requests, and it rarely releases in full
text: DHS's share of all closed requests rose from 18.9% in FY2008 to 60.8% in FY2025. In every year its full-release share (2.4%–12.1%) was below the rest of the government's.
So the government-wide figure looks more and more like DHS's own. Outside DHS, full releases also fell, from 48.7% to 20.7%.

steps.title: A quarter to a half of the national drop comes from DHS handling more of the requests
text: The government-wide full-release share fell 32.1 points from FY2008 to FY2025. A composition decomposition (Kitagawa 1955) splits that fall into three parts. Each bar is the average of two ways of weighting; the thin line is the range between them.
Part of the national decline is a shift toward DHS. But the fall outside DHS is real: 10.9 to 22.7 points whichever way it is weighted. The next steps look outside DHS.
